name: San Francisco Volcanic Field — Cinder Lake Crater Field 1
elevationDescription: 2,050m crater floor basin; surrounding volcanic cinder hills rise to 2,130m
primaryMissionRelevance: Apollo lunar mare cratering, rover terramechanics & Artemis Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV) mobility
geologicalSetting: Quaternary alkali-basalt cinder cones, extensive cinder ash blankets, and basalt lava fields
geomorphology: Man-made crater field blasted with dynamite in 1967 replicating Mare Tranquillitatis crater frequency distribution
environmentalRegime: Semi-arid continental high desert, freeze-thaw cycles, high solar UV flux
operationalHeritage: Historical training site for Apollo 11-17 astronauts, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV) field trials, USGS Grover vehicle

literatureCitations.title: The U.S. Geological Survey Branch of Astrogeology: A Chronological History
Lunar Crater Field Simulation at Cinder Lake, Arizona

name: Iceland Volcanic Highlands — Askja Caldera & Lambahraun
elevationDescription: 1,150m caldera rim; surrounding volcanic plains span 800m to 1,510m
primaryMissionRelevance: Apollo field geology heritage, primitive tholeiitic basalt chemistry, and autonomous obstacle navigation
geologicalSetting: Active Mid-Atlantic plate boundary rift and mantle plume producing primitive tholeiitic basalts and pumice
geomorphology: Caldera collapse scarps, glacio-volcanic palagonite ridges, extensive blocky 'a'ā and ropy pāhoehoe lava fields
environmentalRegime: Subarctic alpine desert, intense precipitation freeze-thaw, zero vegetative canopy
operationalHeritage: Training site for 32 Apollo astronauts (1965/1967) and modern ESA Pangaea field geology campaigns

literatureCitations.title: Apollo Astronaut Training in Iceland: Historic Analogs for Future Lunar Exploration

literatureCitations.title: Iceland as an analog for volcanic and fluvial processes on Mars

name: Atacama Desert — Yungay & Maria Elena South
elevationDescription: 1,100m plateau; hyper-arid core ranges from 900m to 1,300m above sea level
primaryMissionRelevance: Hyper-arid soil chemistry, natural perchlorates, extreme organic carbon depletion, and astrobiological life detection
geologicalSetting: Endorheic tectonic basin filled with evaporitic halite, gypsum, and perchlorate-bearing caliche beds
geomorphology: Playas, salt polygon crusts, yardangs, and deflated wind-scoured gravel plains
environmentalRegime: Hyper-arid (<2mm/year rain), intense UV irradiance (>60 W/m²), extreme desiccation
operationalHeritage: Viking biology instrument benchmark testing, NASA ExoMars drill campaigns, Sample Return caching protocols

literatureCitations.title: Mars-Like Soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the Search for Life
Atmospheric Photochemical Origin of Perchlorate in Atacama and Martian Soils

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys — University & Beacon Valleys
elevationDescription: 1,050m valley floor; ice-free mountain valleys span 500m to 1,600m
primaryMissionRelevance: Dry permafrost equilibrium with atmospheric vapor, cryogenic ground-ice drilling, and polygonal patterned ground
geologicalSetting: Beacon Supergroup quartzose sandstones intruded by Jurassic Ferrar Dolerite sills
geomorphology: Thermal contraction crack polygons (10-30m diameter), ventifacts carved by katabatic winds, and tafoni weathering
environmentalRegime: Hyper-arid polar desert, mean annual temp -20°C to -25°C, winter lows below -50°C, dry permafrost at 10-50cm depth
operationalHeritage: NASA Phoenix lander sub-ice drill testing, IceBite autonomous rotary-percussive drill deployment

literatureCitations.title: Permafrost and Ice-Rich Subsurface on Mars: Antarctic Analogs
Antarctic Dry Valleys: Microclimate zonation, variable geomorphic processes, and implications for Mars

name: Hawaii Volcanic Province — Mauna Kea Summit & HI-SEAS
elevationDescription: 4,207m Mauna Kea summit; HI-SEAS analog habitat located at 2,500m on Mauna Loa flank
primaryMissionRelevance: JSC Mars-1 palagonitic tephra simulant source, basaltic lava tubes for radiation shelter, and human isolation habitat
geologicalSetting: Intraplate oceanic mantle hotspot shield volcano producing tholeiitic and alkalic basalt flows and cinder cones
geomorphology: Pu'u cinder cones, volcanic tephra blankets, intact basaltic lava tube caverns, and high-altitude alpine periglacial slopes
environmentalRegime: High-altitude tropical alpine, low atmospheric humidity, cold night cycling, intense UV solar flux
operationalHeritage: NASA-funded HI-SEAS human crew isolation missions (4-12 months), Apollo lunar navigation, PISCES rover trials

literatureCitations.title: JSC Mars-1: A Martian Regolith Simulant
literatureCitations.citation: Lunar and Planetary Science XXIX, Abstract #1690

literatureCitations.title: HI-SEAS: A Long-Duration Planetary Surface Exploration Simulation

name: Utah Desert & San Rafael Swell — MDRS
elevationDescription: 1,425m elevation; Jurassic sedimentary formations span 1,300m to 1,550m
primaryMissionRelevance: Inverted fluvial channels (Jezero/Eberswalde delta analog), diagenetic hematite Moqui marbles, and Mars Society MDRS ops
geologicalSetting: Mesozoic sedimentary strata (Morrison Formation, Dakota Sandstone, Mancos Shale) deposited in ancient river-floodplain systems
geomorphology: Topographically inverted conglomeratic channel ridges, badlands, bentonite clay swells, and spherical hematite concretions
environmentalRegime: Cold mid-latitude desert, low precipitation, intense seasonal thermal cycling, windy aeolian transport
operationalHeritage: Mars Desert Research Station (MDRS) hosting over 260 field simulation crews since 2001, rover navigation trials

literatureCitations.title: Inverted fluvial channels in the San Rafael Swell, Utah: Analogs for Martian sinuous ridges

name: Devon Island — Haughton-Mars Project (HMP)
elevationDescription: 250m crater floor; complex impact structure spans 100m to 400m elevation
primaryMissionRelevance: Complex impact crater in Paleozoic carbonates, shatter cones, impact-induced hydrothermal systems, and Arctic rover ops
geologicalSetting: 23km diameter meteorite impact crater formed 39 Ma in Ordovician-Silurian limestone and dolomite target strata
geomorphology: Central uplift, polymict impact breccia hills, shatter cones, periglacial thermal contraction polygons, and active-layer gullies
environmentalRegime: Extreme polar desert, continuous permafrost, winter temps below -45°C, degraded magnetic compass environment
operationalHeritage: Haughton-Mars Project (HMP) active since 1997, NASA Ames autonomous humvee/rover testing, field geology drills
